articles.title: Why Trump Quietly Carved Out Doctors From His Own Visa Freeze
articles.content:
自从去年重返执政以来，特朗普总统通过了一系列移民限制措施，他声称这些举措将有利于美国人民。然而，特朗普政府最近修改了一项这样的措施，这一发展表明这项措施可能并未达到预期效果。

据《纽约时报》报道，从1月开始，特朗普政府冻结了对来自39个国家的公民的“签证延期、工作许可和绿卡的审批”。一项总统公告称，需要保护美国人免受“意图实施恐怖袭击、威胁国家安全和公共安全、煽动仇恨犯罪，或以其他恶意方式利用移民法的外国人”。公告还列出了极为狭窄的例外情况——例如，“任何运动员或体育队成员”前往“世界杯、奥运会或其他重要体育赛事”。

然而，到5月，特朗普政府默默承认这项广泛限制并非符合国家利益。《纽约时报》报道称，美国公民及移民服务局悄然更新了其网站，“以表明医生不再受审批暂停的影响”，国土安全部则确认将“恢复为该群体发放签证和工作许可”。

外籍专业人士是美国医疗劳动力的重要组成部分：美国四分之一的医生是国际医学毕业生。农村县和社区尤其依赖外籍医生。在未来十年，随着美国可能面临多达86,000名医生的短缺，外籍医生将显得更加重要。根据美国医学院协会的估计，签证暂停“迫使在美生活多年的医生停止工作，加剧了医院管理者长期头痛的员工短缺问题”，《政客》网站4月份报道称。

不过，外籍医生仍面临诸多障碍。《KFF健康新闻》5月份报道称，由于卫生与公共服务部管理的项目签证豁免申请审批延迟，可能会有“数百名即将在美完成培训的外籍医生不得不立即离开国家”。此外，由于特朗普政府去年秋季推出的10万美元H-1B签证费用，医院也难以赞助国际医生。Axios在3月份指出，“加拿大和其他国家正试图从美国挖角这些医生，提供快速永久居民身份等优惠”。

外籍医生的例外规定是一个积极的进展，但这是对更大问题的狭窄解决方案。模糊的移民限制以决策者无法或不愿想象的方式伤害这个国家。
articles.summary:
Since returning to office last year, President Donald Trump has imposed numerous immigration restrictions that he argues will benefit the American people. The Trump administration recently amended one such measure, a development that suggests it might not be having its intended effect.

Starting in January, the Trump administration froze "decisions on visa extensions, work permits and green cards for citizens of 39 countries," The New York Times reported. A presidential proclamation cited the need to protect Americans "from foreign nationals who intend to commit terrorist attacks, threaten our national security and public safety, incite hate crimes, or otherwise exploit the immigration laws for malevolent purposes." It outlined very narrow exceptions—for example, "any athlete or member of an athletic team" traveling "for the World Cup, Olympics, or other major sporting event."

In May, the Trump administration tacitly admitted this broad restriction is not in the national interest. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services quietly updated its website "to indicate that physicians are no longer subject to the processing hold," and the Department of Homeland Security confirmed that it would "resume issuing visas and work permits for the group," The New York Times reported.

Foreign-born professionals are critical to the country's medical workforce: A quarter of American doctors are international medical graduates. Rural counties and communities are especially dependent on foreign-born physicians. They will prove even more important during the next decade, because the U.S. will face a shortage of up to 86,000 physicians by 2036, according to an estimate from the Association of American Medical Colleges. The visa pause was "forcing physicians who've lived in the U.S. for years to stop working and exacerbating staffing shortages that are a longstanding headache for hospital administrators," Politico reported in April.

Plenty of obstacles remain for foreign doctors. Delays in processing visa waiver applications for a program run by the Department of Health and Human Services could mean that "hundreds of foreign doctors about to complete training in the U.S. will have to leave the country" imminently, KFF Health News reported in May. Hospitals are also having a hard time sponsoring international physicians because of the $100,000 H-1B visa fee that the Trump administration introduced last fall. "Canada and other countries are trying to recruit these doctors away from the U.S., offering incentives like fast-tracked permanent resident status," Axios noted in March.

The foreign doctor carveout is a positive development, but it is a narrow solution to a bigger problem. Imprecise immigration restrictions harm the country in ways that decision makers can't—or won't—imagine.

articles.title: Today in Supreme Court History: August 2, 1923
articles.content:
1923年8月2日：总统卡尔文·库利奇就职。他在任期间将任命哈兰·菲斯克·斯通大法官（Harlan Fiske Stone）进入美国最高法院。

![卡尔文·库利奇总统](https://d2eehagpk5cl65.cloudfront.net/img/q60/uploads/2020/03/Coolidge-225x300.jpg)

*卡尔文·库利奇总统*

（该文章最初发表于《理性》杂志 [Reason.com]）
articles.summary:
8/2/1923: President Calvin Coolidge's Inauguration. He would appoint Justice Harlan Fiske Stone to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Archives: August/September 2026
articles.content:
自2001年9·11恐怖袭击以来的二十年间，REAL ID法案未能得到执行并未使国内航班更易受恐怖袭击威胁。然而，联邦政府和各州至今无法大规模实施REAL ID计划，而普通公众似乎也并未察觉到其必要性。当国会下一次讨论REAL ID的未来时，应考虑废除这一要求。

——斯科特·沙克福德
《即使COVID-19也无法终结REAL ID》

在2001年9·11恐怖袭击之后，美国右翼阵营及部分鹰派自由派一度盛行推崇"美国帝国"的论调，认为通过维持全球霸权可以保护美国免受恐怖主义威胁、遏制反美国家，并保障全球贸易安全。然而，在2000年代中期伊拉克和阿富汗战争持续恶化的背景下，这种好战主义逐渐失宠，仅剩少数坚定的新保守主义者仍在为帝国主义辩护。尽管如此，美国全球军事霸权所引发的问题在公众中仍未得到解决。

——约翰·佩恩
《帝国的诱惑》

如果我们正在以各种方式超越9·11事件，并非因为我们已经处理好了痛苦、恐惧和愤怒，而是因为我们已开始遗忘它曾经发生过。最多再过十年，我们将会像漫步经过全国各地小镇广场上的第一次世界大战纪念碑那样，经过9·11纪念馆。宣泄情感？算了吧；这或许正是我们总是超越创伤的方式。压抑和历史失忆是上帝或进化赋予我们最强大的工具之一。

——尼克·吉尔斯皮
《9·11之后艺术为什么失败了》

回顾9·11袭击后最初的几天和几周里那些为数不多的亮点，几乎没有任何一件是源自政治家或有影响力的人物。美国十年前所展示的力量并非来自于华盛顿的新官僚机构集中化、联邦雇员的联合化，或政府更轻松地监视甚至杀害本国公民的能力。这种力量源于个体，源于习惯于自由生活的人们以分散的方式行动，使一场可怕的事件略微减轻痛苦。其中有一个重要的教训值得学习。

——马特·威尔奇
《一切继续改变的日子》

联邦通信委员会的任务几乎不可能完成；它无法监管全国数千家许可持有者，确保他们遵守授予的特许权。由于缺乏整体概念框架，它无法理性应对技术进步，而技术进步总是超越并超出其制定的政治和司法规则和规定的范围。

——迈克尔·布鲁姆
《数据通信之战》

1888年民主党政党纲领将关税和配额称为"垄断之母"。当时著名的信托（如糖和烟草业）受到外国竞争的保护。当时的智者论证称，自由贸易将通过允许全世界为美国消费者的业务竞争来保护美国消费者。垄断全球某一产品的生产要比垄断一个国家市场难得多。当巴西试图限制其咖啡销售以提高价格时，她只成功地促使其他国家种植咖啡，导致咖啡产量增加，价格比以前更低。

——罗德·曼尼斯
《自由企业与垄断神话》
articles.summary:
5 years ago
Aug/Sept 2021

"In the two decades since the September 11 attacks, the absence of REAL ID enforcement has not made domestic flights more vulnerable to terrorism. Meanwhile, the federal government and the states have not been able to implement REAL ID at scale, and the general public does not seem to see a need for it. The next time Congress debates the future of REAL ID, it should repeal the requirement for good."
Scott Shackford
"Even COVID-19 Couldn't Kill  REAL ID"

15 years ago
Aug/Sept 2011

"After the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, it became fashionable on the right, and among some hawkish liberals, to defend and even promote the idea of an American Empire to keep us safe from terrorists, hold rogue nations in check, and secure global commerce…..In the middle years of the last decade, as the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan grew steadily worse, this jingoism fell out of favor, leaving only a shrinking core of committed neoconservatives to champion the virtues of empire. Still, the questions posed by American global military dominance were far from settled in public opinion."
John Payne
"Temptations of Empire"

"If we are getting over 9/11 in ways big and small, it's not because we have worked through the pain and the terror and the anger but simply because we are forgetting it ever happened in the first place. Within another decade at most, we will walk by 9/11 memorials the same way we stroll by the World War I cenotaphs installed in town squares across the country. Catharsis be damned; this is probably the way we always get over trauma. Repression and historical amnesia are among the most powerful tools God or evolution has handed us."

Nick Gillespie
"Why Art Failed Us After 9/11"

"Looking back at the few bright moments during those first days and weeks after the attacks, I can think of hardly any that emanated from a politician or figure of influence….The strength of America on display 10 years ago did not result from centralizing new bureaucracies in Washington, unionizing new sets of federal employees, or devising easier ways for the government to snoop on and even kill its own citizens. It came from individual human beings, accustomed to living in freedom, acting in a decentralized manner to make an atrocious event slightly less painful. There's an important lesson there, waiting to be learned."
Matt Welch
"The Day Everything Continued To Change"

55 years ago
September 1971

"The [Federal Communications] Commission has an impossible job; it cannot police the thousands of licensees across the nation to ensure that they remain within the charters granted them. Lacking an overall conceptual framework, it cannot respond rationally to the technological advances which continually outpace and outscope the political and jurisdictional rules and regulations it sets forth."
Michael Bloom
"The Data Communications Battle"

"The Democratic Party Platform of 1888 called tariffs and quotas the 'mother of monopoly.' The famous trusts of the time (e.g., sugar and tobacco) were protected from foreign competition. It was wisely argued that free trade would protect the American consumer by allowing the whole world to compete for his business. Monopolizing the world production of a product is infinitely more difficult than monopolizing a national market. When Brazil tried to restrict her coffee sales to raise prices, she only succeeded in causing coffee to be grown in other countries, which meant greater production and lower prices than before."
Rod Manis
"Free Enterprise and the Monopoly Myth"

articles.title: Today in Supreme Court History: August 1, 1942
articles.content:
1942年8月1日：八名纳粹特工的军事法庭审判结束。最高法院在《Ex Parte Quirin》案中支持了这些审判的合宪性。

（1942年最高法院）
[图片：石法庭（1942年）]

本文最初发表于Reason.com网站，标题为《今日最高法院历史：1942年8月1日》。
articles.summary:
8/1/1942: Military commissions conclude for eight nazi saboteurs. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of these trials in Ex Parte Quirin.
